verdict.rationale: Skyfire implements a mandate-style consent mechanism: pay/kya-pay tokens are signed, interoperable JWT credentials that commit a specific spending amount against the buyer's wallet at creation time, and charges above that committed ceiling are rejected (skyfire-supp-3, skyfire-supp-4). Cardholder consent is explicitly bounded — 'the agent/agent platform can never spend more than the cardholder approved,' with the authorized amount as a hard ceiling (skyfire-supp-7) — and KYA verification gates which services can even be transacted with (skyfire-supp-2). However, there is no documented interactive human confirmation step at the moment of each purchase (e.g., a push notification or click-to-approve UI) — the mandate is created programmatically by the agent itself, and revocation of in-flight tokens isn't supported once issued (skyfire-supp-6). Missing for 10: an explicit human-in-the-loop confirmation/approval UI per purchase, and documented ability to revoke/cancel an issued mandate before settlement.
